methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $52M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Kinova Robotics is a late-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Charles Deguire and Louis-Joseph L'Ecuyer that has raised $51.6M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of nine private robotics peers (including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics) and one public comparable (277810.KQ), though peer-median analysis proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage datapoints within the narrow robotics set.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised of $51.6M as a baseline valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage advancement, this method implies a valuation of $62M. This represents a single-method analysis given constraints on peer density and specificity.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $53M (low) to $71M (high), centered on a $62M median. The low bound reflects the raised capital floor; the high bound incorporates modest upside from stage progression logic. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight stage-matched comparables in the robotics sector, limiting confidence in capital-efficiency benchmarking. Revenue scale, unit economics, and customer concentration—standard late-stage metrics—are not available in the dataset, and would materially inform any refined valuation. The single-method result suggests material sensitivity to refinement via additional comparable data or operational metrics.
